The lower bound argument is sound: any non‑constant map \(C\to A_i\) forces the induced homomorphism \(\operatorname{Jac}(C)\to A_i\) to be surjective because each \(A_i\) is simple. Since the image of \(\operatorname{Jac}(C)\) in the product must project onto both simple factors, it must be the whole product, so \(\dim\operatorname{Jac}(C)=g(C)\ge 4\).

The existence part is also valid. The moduli space of principally polarized abelian fourfolds (Jacobians of genus‑4 curves) is 9‑dimensional, while the space of products of two very general abelian surfaces (up to isogeny) also has the same dimension, and the Prym construction shows that a generic product \(A_1\times A_2\) is isogenous to the Jacobian of a suitable genus‑4 curve. Hence a curve of genus 4 with both non‑constant projections does exist, proving the bound is sharp.

Therefore the minimal possible genus is indeed 4.
